work.author: Severian of Gabala
work.title: In illud: in principium erat verbum

paragraphs.text: Yesterday our sermon came to rest in contemplating the great eagle. He is truly a great eagle: in the Spirit he soared beyond heaven and the powers above the world, and he began from the very summit of all things. For John proclaimed to us beforehand, "In the beginning was the Word," and set out the true philosophy of the uncreated nature. He rose above the whole of creation, higher than any eagle's nature can go. He surpassed the sound of every thunder too, since he alone proclaimed the eternal philosophy that is above the world. Thunder, beloved, both frightens and waters. It waters through the clouds, and through its voice it frightens and astounds. In the same way John's voice divides its work: it waters the church, and it astounds the faction of the heretics. They speak vain things. They know the things that are, yet they dare to say that these are not. They marshal human argument against divine Scripture. Then John cries out his "was" against their "was not": "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." His voice astounds his opponents, and David bears witness, saying: "At your rebuke they will flee; at the voice of your thunder they will be afraid." "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." Because the begetting of the Word is free of passion, he says "Word," so that from what belongs to you he may teach you what is beyond you. The mind begets a word without passion. It is not cut, it does not flow out, and it undergoes nothing else of what bodies undergo. In the same way the divine and passionless begetting is unspeakable and incomprehensible. It is not cut and not divided, though the impious and faithless heretics wickedly cut it, while true piety rightly holds it united. Why did the evangelist avoid saying "In the beginning was the Son"? So that the name "Son" would not suggest a begetting with passion. Instead he calls him "Word," to show that the begetting is without passion. And so that you would not think of a spoken word, he added, "and the Word was God." From "Word" you understand that he was begotten without passion, and from "God" you understand his dignity. Then, after setting out what concerns his begetting, he also introduces the high dignity of his power to create: "All things came into being through him." This means all things that have come into being. It does not mean what the children of the heretics claim, when they dare to include even the adorable Spirit in this phrase. "All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being that has come into being in him." So if anything has come into being in him, that is not the uncreated nature of the Spirit. "But," he objects, "it says 'all things.'" Yet the word "all things" does not include the uncreated nature along with the created. If you fasten on the word "all" and dare to attack the holy nature, what will you say when you hear the Lord saying, "All who came before me were thieves and robbers"? Do you call Moses a robber, and name the prophets thieves? For he says, "All who came before me were thieves and robbers." But the sense shows whom the statement concerns and to whom it is addressed. Here too the statement concerns creation. It says that creation came into being through him, not the essence of the Spirit. The Spirit knows the things of God just as a man's spirit knows what is in him, as Paul says: "No one knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that dwells in him." If, then, my spirit is foreign to my nature, then the Spirit of God is also foreign to God's nature. "For the Spirit," he says, "searches all things, even the depths of God." The heretic hears "searches" and takes its meaning wrongly. "If the Spirit knew the things in God," he says, "he would not search. The searching proves his ignorance." Suppose the Holy Spirit's searching of the depths of God charges him with ignorance. Then when you see God searching the hearts of men, will you condemn him for ignorance too? Listen to Paul. He said of the Spirit, "The Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God." In the same way Paul says when he speaks of God: "He who searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit." If God searches because he does not know, then the Spirit too searches because he does not know. But Paul wanted you to learn that searching belongs to one who knows, not to one who is ignorant. So he added: "So too no one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God." He ascribes knowledge to the Spirit: not a comprehension [?] from nature, but a knowledge that springs from his nature.

So do not divide the indivisible nature, and do not cut the undivided essence. Instead, recognize its power precisely. The Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are called one. For the Son says of the Father: "When you see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power." By saying "Power" he established the Father's glory, so that you might marvel at what this means. So he called the Father and God himself "Power" when he spoke with Caiaphas: "When you see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power." The Father, then, is power. The Son is also power, as Paul says: "Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God." And the Holy Spirit is power, for the Savior says to the disciples: "Stay in Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high." Beloved, now that you know this same power is in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, keep your faith unshaken. Do not divide the incomprehensible glory. Recognize instead the covenant of illumination. See the sons of grace who have blossomed through the great high priest. See the children of the light running to the heralds of the light. Those reborn through illumination must run to those who gave new birth to the world. Let us too say with the prophet and the apostles: "Lift up your eyes and see your children gathered together." And again: "As I live, says the Lord, you shall put them all on like a bride's adornment." So today Isaiah stands and speaks to the crowds of the newly illumined. They were born of the Holy Spirit, renewed all at once and changed in a single instant, transformed from an earthly condition into a heavenly image. Isaiah is amazed and says: "Who has seen, who has heard such things, that the earth has given birth to her children in one day, and a nation has been born at once?" For the Spirit's rebirth is swift. It does not wait for time, and it is not a slave to seasons and generations. The moment it wills, the one being reborn is born. It would have been fitting for the sons of light to process through the whole marketplace, to glorify and acclaim him who came down below for their sake to lead the whole world up to himself on high. Christ came down from heaven. He came down without leaving heaven, and he went up without leaving the earth. In coming down he did not leave the heavens empty, and in going up he did not leave the earth without his care. It would have been fitting for the sons of light to carry the torch of the Word around the marketplaces. The mystery would not have been insulted, and the stamp of truth on the newly illumined would not have been dishonored. It would also have been fitting for them to sing hymns in the streets. For wisdom is hymned in the ways out, she speaks boldly in the streets, and she is proclaimed on the tops of the walls. Let us purify the air that lewd songs defiled, that the shouts of the impious once stained, along with the shrieks of those who performed the foul rites of demons. The word of light has cleansed the air, the earth and heaven. Heaven and earth groan at the wickedness of the impious, and in the same way they rejoice again at the righteousness of those who do well. When a man sins, heaven is indignant and the earth is indignant, as Jeremiah says: "Heaven was astonished at this, and the earth shuddered, because the people have committed two evils." Do you see how heaven and earth shudder when people sin? But when they change themselves toward piety, listen to the prophet: "Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice. Let the mountains break out in gladness and the hills in exultation, for God has had mercy on his people." Let the church, which flourishes with so great a crowd and people, say too: "Once I was left alone; where were these for me then? I was childless and a widow; who bore these for me?" And let the children of the church, hemmed in by the multitude, say to God the words of the prophets: "The place is too narrow for me; make room for me, so that I may dwell."

When error was at its height, when heresy was spreading through this city like a grazing herd, the children of the church were being consumed. A locust comes upon the land under heaven and devours its fruits. In the same way the corrupting teaching devoured the fruits of true teaching and of piety. But today, beloved, the corrupting teaching has been driven out. Saving grace has come in, giving the people new birth and saying to them: "Now I will repay you for the offspring that the caterpillar, the locust and the blight devoured." Why, heretic, are you striving with the Jews to hide the glory of the Only-begotten? They hid the resurrection, as far as it lay in their power. You hide his divinity, as far as it lies in yours. But they do not accept the truth, and you have not understood piety. Listen to the prophet: "His virtue covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise." Of his praise, not of comprehending him. Of faith, not of scrutiny. Of love, not of inquiry. We were not taught to inquire; we were trained to believe. We are illumined by believing, and we are not baptized by prying curiosity. Do not let the assemblies of the heretics deceive you. They have baptism, but not illumination. They are baptized in body, but in soul they are not illumined. Simon was baptized but not illumined, and they turn out to be the same. So let the spirits of the apostles rejoice, who through the Holy Spirit have caught this great people in the spiritual net. Now the prophet's words have been fulfilled before our eyes: "In the last days, says God, they shall no longer say, 'Behold the ark of the covenant of the Holy One of Israel'" (that is, the old worship), "nor shall the covenant of the ark come into their heart." Why? "Because behold, I am sending many hunters and fishers." He set aside the old ark and brought in the ark of the church, which does not perish. "I am sending many hunters and fishers." What strange fishing! The one caught yesterday is fishing today. For the earth has been filled with the glory of Christ, and the ends of the world have been filled with faith. So do not insult his dignity because of the dispensation. Among the Jews the story went out that the resurrection had been bought, and the story went out that his disciples had stolen him. They declared death over his body, and these people, as far as they can, [?] his divinity. But error holds sway among them today, while in the church eternal life is proclaimed. If you like, you also have an ancient image of this. When his brothers plotted against Joseph, Jacob and his household mourned him bitterly, but Egypt had him alive and reigning. Jacob mourned him as dead, while in Egypt he lived and reigned. So now too the synagogue and the madness of the heretics think him dead. For those who do away with faith and bring in inquiry make his divinity dead. But among us he lives and reigns, and is worshipped as he deserves. Truly the word of God is mighty, and the teaching of the apostles is invincible. So Paul's voice, which pleaded for the truth, does not labor in vain. Speak then, blessed Paul, moved on behalf of the truth! Be indignant for the faith, and in your indignation say to the heretics: "Where were you taught these Aristotelian things? Who put Plato above the Gospels? Who threw out the proclamation of faith and brought in faithless inquiry? Where did you learn 'unbegotten' and 'begotten'? You have abandoned 'Father,' you have spat on the name 'Son,' you have thought the dignity of the Spirit unworthy, and you turn to human words." Jeremiah put it well: "Faith has perished from their mouth." What did Peter say, for which he was called blessed? "You are the Christ, the Son of God." He did not say, "You are the offspring of the Unbegotten," but "You are the Christ, the Son of God." When the Father was revealing wisdom to him, did he not know how to grasp it? Could Christ not have said to the apostles, when he commanded them to baptize, "Go and baptize the nations in the name of the Unbegotten and the Begotten"? But he has found a name wiser than the mystical traditions! You confine divine things within limits, you do away with faith and bring in inquiry. But be afraid, enemy: Peter holds the keys. He received the keys because he said, "You are the Christ, the Son of God." To those he sees calling him Son, Peter opens the door of the kingdom. To all he finds calling him a creature and blaspheming, he shuts the door of the church. He did not receive the keys until he had said, "You are the Son of God." Then he in turn hears from him: "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah; to you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven." After the confession came the authority. After the faith came the handing over of the church and the kingdom.

Some make war against the Son, and others draw up their ranks against the Holy Spirit. But it is no use confessing Christ while rejecting the Holy Spirit, just as it is no use confessing the Father while rejecting the Son. The Jews too confess the Father while denying the Son, and they do not have eternal life. Whoever disregards the glory of the Son is not acceptable to the Father. Pay close attention. Job's friends took God's side and condemned Job. Yet God did not accept even those who argued on his behalf, but said: "Why have you spoken against my servant Job?" He did not accept the friends who glorified him while speaking against Job. Will he ever accept those who confess him while rejecting the Son? By no means. For he says, "Whoever hates me hates my Father also." The Father does not accept honor paid to him when the Son is rejected. In the same way neither the Father nor the Son accepts it when the Holy Spirit is rejected. Paul himself found heretical weeds that had begun to sprout, though they never gained free rein. In Ephesus in Asia he finds some people who had been baptized, and he says to them: "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" They said, "We have not even heard whether there is a Holy Spirit." Then came that noble voice: "Into what, then, were you baptized?" Let Peter and Paul teach the church not to weave heretical disputes. Where did the ill-omened name of Eunomius come from? Where did the heretical seeds come from? Truly the truth has perished among the impious, and Aristotelian teaching has prevailed. Do you take the categories of human nature and apply them to the divine, and say "unbegotten" and "begotten"? "But you," he says, "what do you call the Father?" I call him unbegotten, but not as you do. I call the Father unbegotten because he was not begotten. But I also call Adam unbegotten, since he was not begotten but formed. Let this not startle the hearers: these are things that were formed. The Father is unbegotten, and many other things are unbegotten too. Everything that has not been begotten is called unbegotten. Everything that is coming to be but has not yet come to be is also called unbegotten. The resurrection of the dead is unbegotten now: it is coming, but it has not yet happened, and it is not yet made ready, not yet begotten. What never comes to be and is never meant to come to be is also called unbegotten, and there are many such unbegotten things. Take the prophets. Daniel says: "I saw four beasts coming up out of the sea, and the first beast was like a lioness, and its wings were like an eagle's." Tell me, where have you ever seen a lioness built like that? Where have you seen a beast with iron claws and bronze teeth? The prophet shaped these things for a vision. They did not come to be and do not come to be. That beast is unbegotten: it never came into being, and was only named. What women ever existed with wings, like the winged women Zechariah knows of? Where have you seen a leopard with wings? Yet the blessed Daniel describes all these. Or where have you seen a statue made of gold and silver and bronze and iron and clay, like the one Daniel saw? Each of these is unbegotten, for it never came into being. It was written down as an image and a vision. So do not think you are granting the Father anything great by calling him unbegotten, since many other things that were never begotten are called unbegotten. I know the argument is deep, but I have entered this ground to refute the malice of the heretics. A man who was not born is also called unbegotten. "And if he was not born," he says, "how can he be spoken of?" I will show you a man who was not born. The Savior says of Judas the traitor: "Woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed. It would have been better for him if he had not been born." And how would it have been better for him? Nothing either benefits or harms what does not exist. Solomon too calls blessed the man who was not born, saying: "Blessed is the dead rather than the living, and better than both is the one who was not born." And if he was not born, how is he blessed? See here names of an unbegotten nature: he called blessed a man who was neither born nor formed. So the name "unbegotten" does not express a divine nature, nor does it mean what you say. It [does not?] signify an unbegotten essence, and it brings no honor to the Father, since, as was shown above, the prophet has other names of things both unbegotten and begotten. It shows only that something has not come into being. But let us say to them with David: "The lawless have told me idle tales, but they are not like your law, O Lord." Accept the voice of Peter and the teaching of Paul: "Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all, blessed forever." Let the Holy Spirit be worshipped, hymned and glorified. We speak of God from the divine Scriptures, whether our enemies like it or not. Paul will bear me witness, saying: "Do you not know that you are God's temple?" And who dwells in it? "And the Spirit of God dwells in you." So the temple is one thing, and the one who dwells in it is another. Have you not heard Peter saying: "Ananias, why has Satan tempted your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit?" And he added: "You have not lied to men but to God." The heretics say that he did not call the Spirit God, but spoke this way because the Spirit was sent from God. "Whoever insults the Spirit," he says, "insults God, who sent the Spirit." You senseless, irrational man! No other name befits the godless except "fool," for "the fool has said in his heart, 'There is no God.'" Peter did not mean what you have taken him to mean. If the insult to the Spirit went back to God as the one who sent him, he would have had to say, "You have not lied to the Spirit but to God." But enough of this. We must now give way to the apostolic choir, the holy triad whom our father announces, a triad of apostles bearing witness to the heavenly Trinity. So let us join the dance with sincere hearts and say: "Many are the children of the desolate woman, more than of her who has a husband." That is, more than every heresy that has a man as its teacher and not God. Through the prayers and intercessions of our common father and teacher, may we all dwell together with apostles and martyrs in the orthodox faith, in Christ Jesus our Lord. To him be glory and might, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.
